meta.tier_interpretation_note: These tiers reflect salinity conditions (electrical conductivity, EC) at the Banks (SWP) and Jones (CVP) Delta export pumps across months and years. Likelihood scores reflect policy-to-outcome plausibility—i.e., how strongly each legal standard can drive or constrain operations that affect export-area salinity—not a guarantee of achieving any tier.

notes_on_metrics.ec_units: uS/cm (EC normalized to 25°C is commonly used in standards and monitoring)
sites: Harvey O. Banks Pumping Plant (State Water Project export)
C.W. 'Bill' Jones Pumping Plant (Central Valley Project export)

Legal Standards.name: SWRCB Water Quality Control Plan for the San Francisco Bay/Sacramento–San Joaquin Delta Estuary (Bay-Delta Plan)
Legal Standards.note: Establishes beneficial uses and enforceable water quality objectives (including salinity/EC objectives) and a program of implementation. These objectives are a primary legal lever for managing Delta conditions relevant to salinity at/near export facilities.

key_elements.plain_definition: A state plan that identifies beneficial uses to protect and sets water-quality goals (objectives) plus actions for meeting them.
A numeric or narrative target (e.g., salinity/EC limit) intended to protect a beneficial use.
A recognized use of water (e.g., agricultural supply, municipal supply, fish/wildlife) that standards are designed to protect.
The set of actions/requirements used to meet the objectives (often includes flow and operational requirements).
Saltier ocean water pushing inland into the Delta when freshwater flows are insufficient.

sources: https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/waterrights/water_issues/programs/compliance_monitoring/sacramento_sanjoaquin/ (Bay-Delta Plan overview and D-1641 compliance context)

Legal Standards.name: SWRCB Water Right Decision 1641 (D-1641) implementing Bay-Delta Plan objectives for CVP/SWP operations (1999; as amended/used in compliance)
Legal Standards.note: Implements Bay-Delta Plan water quality objectives through water right terms/conditions for the CVP and SWP, including operational responsibilities to meet salinity-related objectives at compliance locations relevant to export operations.

key_elements.plain_definition: A monitoring point where water quality is measured to determine whether objectives are being met.
Pumping/diversion of Delta water at Banks (SWP) and Jones (CVP) facilities.
When monitored salinity/EC goes above the allowed limit at a compliance location.

Legal Standards.name: Porter-Cologne Water Quality Control Act (California Water Code §13000 et seq.)
Legal Standards.note: Core California water quality statute giving the Water Boards authority to adopt and implement water quality control plans (like the Bay-Delta Plan) and enforce water quality objectives that include salinity protections for agricultural and municipal uses in the Delta.

key_elements.plain_definition: California’s State Water Resources Control Board plus nine Regional Boards that set and enforce water quality rules.
A regional water quality plan; the Bay-Delta Plan is a statewide plan for the Bay-Delta system.

sources: https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/plans_policies/docs/2018wqcp.pdf (Bay-Delta Plan document context referencing Porter-Cologne framework)

Legal Standards.name: Federal Clean Water Act (CWA) — water quality standards + Section 401 certification (33 U.S.C. §1251 et seq.)
Legal Standards.note: Federal law under which state-adopted water quality standards (beneficial uses + objectives) are recognized, and Section 401 requires state certification (often with conditions) for federally permitted/licensed activities that may discharge to waters. Can influence projects/actions affecting Delta salinity conditions (e.g., conveyance, barriers, habitat projects, dredge/fill, hydropower-related actions upstream).

key_elements.plain_definition: In Clean Water Act terms, the combination of beneficial uses and water quality objectives that must be protected.
State must certify a federally permitted/licensed project will comply with water quality standards; the state can add enforceable conditions or deny.

Legal Standards.name: Sacramento–San Joaquin Delta Reform Act of 2009 (Water Code §85000 et seq.)
Legal Standards.note: Creates the Delta Stewardship Council and embeds the ‘coequal goals’ (including ecosystem protection/restoration) into Delta governance. It can constrain or shape state actions (and major Delta projects) via Delta Plan consistency, indirectly affecting the policy environment around export operations and salinity management.

key_elements.plain_definition: State policy goals to both provide a more reliable water supply for California and protect, restore, and enhance the Delta ecosystem.
A process where certain covered actions must be consistent with the Delta Plan’s policies.

Legal Standards.name: Federal Endangered Species Act (ESA) (16 U.S.C. §1531 et seq.)
Legal Standards.note: While not a salinity standard, ESA can strongly constrain CVP/SWP export operations (e.g., to protect listed species). Those operational constraints can indirectly change Delta outflow/flow patterns and therefore influence salinity near export pumps and at compliance locations.

key_elements.plain_definition: Federal agencies must consult to ensure actions don’t jeopardize listed species; resulting Biological Opinions can require operational changes.

Legal Standards.name: Central Valley Project Improvement Act (CVPIA) (1992) (Pub. L. 102-575, Title XXXIV)
Legal Standards.note: Federal law requiring operational and restoration improvements for fish and wildlife connected to the CVP. Like ESA, CVPIA constraints can indirectly affect export operations and Delta flow patterns relevant to salinity outcomes, particularly in dry years or when environmental allocations become binding.

key_elements.plain_definition: Water reserved/managed for environmental purposes (e.g., fish and habitat), which can reduce operational flexibility for exports.

Legal Standards.name: California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) (Pub. Res. Code §21000 et seq.)
Legal Standards.note: Procedural law requiring disclosure of environmental impacts and adoption of feasible mitigation/alternatives for discretionary projects. CEQA can shape Delta conveyance, barriers, or operational-change projects that affect salinity (but it does not set salinity thresholds itself).

key_elements.plain_definition: Measures to reduce significant environmental impacts of a project.
Evaluation of different ways to meet a project’s goals with fewer impacts.

sources: https://opr.ca.gov/ceqa/ (California Office of Planning and Research CEQA portal)

Tier 1.threshold: Average of both Banks & Jones salinity is below 900 uS/cm for all 12 months per year for 95% of years

policies.policy_name: Bay-Delta Plan (SWRCB Water Quality Control Plan)
policies.relationship: Direct salinity/EC objectives and implementation framework aligned with achieving Tier 1 conditions
policies.note: Mechanism: The Plan sets enforceable salinity-related objectives and an implementation program that can require flow and operational conditions (including export and reservoir operations) that reduce salinity intrusion, supporting consistently low EC at/near export-relevant locations.

policies.policy_name: D-1641 (implementation of Bay-Delta objectives through CVP/SWP water right conditions)
policies.relationship: Direct operational leverage on CVP/SWP exports/operations to meet salinity-related objectives
policies.note: Mechanism: Translates plan objectives into enforceable operating terms for CVP/SWP; compliance monitoring and operational requirements are a primary lever to keep export-area salinity below stringent levels across most months/years.

policies.relationship: Foundational authority enabling Tier 1-relevant objectives, but indirect by itself
policies.note: Mechanism: Grants authority to adopt/enforce plans and objectives; actual Tier 1 performance depends on the specific objectives/implementation measures adopted (e.g., Bay-Delta Plan + D-1641) and enforcement.

policies.relationship: Conditional influence via standards recognition and permitting/certification of activities affecting Delta conditions
policies.note: Mechanism: CWA anchors the concept of water quality standards and allows the state to condition/deny certain federally permitted actions via §401; this can protect conditions that influence salinity, but it is not the main day-to-day export salinity control lever.

policies.relationship: Indirect—species-driven export constraints may improve salinity conditions in some scenarios
policies.note: Mechanism: ESA-required operational constraints on exports (to protect listed species) can increase net Delta outflow or alter flow patterns, which can reduce salinity intrusion; however, effects on EC at Banks/Jones are contingent on hydrology and operations.

policies.relationship: Indirect—environmental allocations/operations may reduce export-driven salinity stress in some conditions
policies.note: Mechanism: Fish-and-wildlife operational requirements can reduce export flexibility and alter reservoir/flow operations, potentially supporting fresher conditions, but salinity outcomes remain highly hydrology-dependent.

policies.policy_name: Delta Reform Act / Delta Plan consistency
policies.relationship: Governance lever—may indirectly favor salinity-protective actions but not an operational salinity standard
policies.note: Mechanism: Consistency policies can shape major Delta actions and planning priorities; influence on Tier 1 salinity outcomes is indirect and contingent on specific covered actions and how policies are applied.

policies.relationship: Procedural—can shape projects that affect salinity but does not set/export-operate to EC thresholds
policies.note: Mechanism: CEQA can require mitigation/alternatives for projects that could worsen salinity intrusion (or enable projects that improve conditions), but achieving Tier 1 is not a mandated CEQA outcome.

Tier 2.threshold: Average of Banks and Jones salinity is between 900 and 1600 uS/cm for at least 10 months per year for 95% of years

policies.policy_name: Bay-Delta Plan (SWRCB Water Quality Control Plan)
policies.relationship: Direct objectives/implementation can plausibly maintain Tier 2 performance in many hydrologic conditions
policies.note: Mechanism: Objectives and implementation measures can maintain acceptable salinity conditions for most months in most years, particularly if flow/operation requirements are designed to protect agricultural and municipal uses.

policies.relationship: Direct operational lever for keeping export-area salinity within Tier 2 ranges across most months/years
policies.note: Mechanism: Enforceable operating conditions and compliance monitoring can prevent frequent high-EC months by constraining exports and coordinating reservoir releases/outflow when required.

policies.relationship: Enabling authority; Tier 2 depends on specific plan objectives/enforcement choices
policies.note: Mechanism: Supports setting and enforcing objectives for agricultural/municipal beneficial uses; the degree of Tier 2 protection is conditional on adopted objectives and implementation rigor.

policies.relationship: Conditional influence via permits/certifications and federal recognition of standards
policies.note: Mechanism: §401 can impose enforceable conditions on federally permitted actions that might worsen salinity dynamics; influence is project-by-project rather than continuous export-ops control.

policies.relationship: Indirect—species protections may incidentally support Tier 2 by constraining exports during sensitive periods
policies.note: Mechanism: Export constraints for listed species can sometimes increase outflow or reduce reverse flows that contribute to salinity intrusion; effect varies by year and operational regime.

policies.relationship: Indirect—fish-focused operational/restoration measures can shift operations in ways that sometimes support Tier 2
policies.note: Mechanism: CVP operational requirements may reduce export flexibility and influence flow releases, which can help maintain moderate salinity conditions in some periods.

policies.policy_name: Delta Reform Act / Delta Plan consistency
policies.relationship: Indirect governance influence
policies.note: Mechanism: Can shape major projects and policies affecting Delta hydrodynamics; not a direct salinity standard and outcomes are contingent on specific actions.

policies.relationship: Indirect procedural influence
policies.note: Mechanism: Can require mitigation for projects that could worsen salinity; does not provide operational control to reliably produce Tier 2 across most years.

Tier 3.threshold: Average of Banks and Jones salinity is above 1600 uS/cm for 2 or more months in any year, or in more than 5% of years at either site

policies.policy_name: Bay-Delta Plan (SWRCB Water Quality Control Plan)
policies.relationship: Tier 3 conditions suggest objectives/implementation may be insufficient or not met (depending on which objectives apply at which locations)
policies.note: Mechanism: If Tier 3 conditions occur, Bay-Delta objectives and implementation tools are the most direct legal route for tightening standards, changing compliance requirements, or requiring operational responses (flows/outflow/export constraints) to reduce high-EC months.

policies.relationship: Tier 3 conditions can indicate operational non-attainment or hydrologic stress; D-1641 compliance/enforcement is a direct lever
policies.note: Mechanism: Compliance monitoring and enforceable operating terms can trigger operational adjustments (or highlight inability to comply in extreme conditions), making D-1641 central to addressing repeated high-EC months.

policies.relationship: Foundational enforcement and planning authority for responding to Tier 3 trends
policies.note: Mechanism: Enables Water Boards to revise objectives/programs and enforce requirements; response strength depends on adopted standards and enforcement posture.

policies.relationship: Conditional—can prevent worsening from specific federally permitted actions; not a primary lever for export salinity operations
policies.note: Mechanism: §401 can constrain projects that would exacerbate salinity intrusion or degrade related water quality; does not directly set CVP/SWP monthly export salinity outcomes.

policies.relationship: Indirect—species constraints may reduce exports or change flows during periods that overlap with high salinity risk
policies.note: Mechanism: ESA-driven reductions in exports or changed flow patterns can sometimes reduce salinity intrusion, but Tier 3 is driven heavily by hydrology and ocean/Delta dynamics.

policies.relationship: Indirect—may affect operations in ways that reduce salinity stress in some cases
policies.note: Mechanism: Environmental allocations/requirements can constrain exports and influence reservoir release patterns, potentially reducing the frequency of high-EC months in some years.

policies.policy_name: Delta Reform Act / Delta Plan consistency
policies.relationship: Tier 3 conditions can elevate governance pressure for ecosystem/water quality alignment, but operational effects are indirect
policies.note: Mechanism: Indirectly shapes major Delta decisions that could influence salinity drivers (e.g., conveyance/hydrodynamics), but does not itself operate pumps or set EC limits.

policies.relationship: Tier 3 conditions may increase scrutiny of projects affecting Delta hydrodynamics/salinity, but effects are contingent
policies.note: Mechanism: CEQA can force stronger mitigation/alternatives for projects that worsen salinity; still not a direct operational control mechanism.

Tier 4.threshold: Average of Banks and Jones salinity is greater than 2500 uS/cm for 2 or more months in any year

policies.policy_name: Bay-Delta Plan (SWRCB Water Quality Control Plan)
policies.relationship: Tier 4 indicates extreme salinity conditions; Bay-Delta objectives/implementation are the strongest legal levers for requiring protective operational responses or revising standards/programs
policies.note: Mechanism: Extreme EC conditions heighten the role of enforceable objectives and implementation requirements (e.g., flow/outflow/export constraints, coordinated operations) to reduce salinity intrusion where feasible.

policies.relationship: Direct—central compliance/enforcement framework for CVP/SWP operations under stress
policies.note: Mechanism: Provides operational terms and compliance monitoring for the export projects; during extreme conditions, D-1641 is the most immediate legal hook for operational requirements (or documenting inability to meet objectives).

policies.relationship: Foundational enforcement/planning authority; indirect by itself
policies.note: Mechanism: Authorizes Water Boards to enforce requirements and revise plans/objectives; Tier 4 responses depend on the specific implementation measures the Boards impose.

policies.relationship: Conditional—can restrict certain projects that worsen conditions; not primary for month-to-month export salinity control
policies.note: Mechanism: §401 conditions/denials can prevent additional degradation from federally permitted actions, but Tier 4 is most directly driven by hydrology and export/outflow operations under state planning and water-right terms.

policies.relationship: Indirect—species-based export constraints may reduce exports and sometimes help salinity outcomes, but effects are contingent
policies.note: Mechanism: ESA constraints can reduce exports or require flow actions that might counter salinity intrusion in some cases; Tier 4 exceedances can still occur during extreme drought/low inflow despite species protections.

policies.relationship: Indirect—may constrain exports or influence releases; outcome effects vary
policies.note: Mechanism: CVPIA fish/wildlife requirements can affect how CVP is operated in dry periods; salinity benefits are plausible but not assured.

policies.policy_name: Delta Reform Act / Delta Plan consistency
policies.relationship: Indirect governance influence under extreme conditions
policies.note: Mechanism: Can influence long-term structural responses (planning, conveyance decisions), but does not provide immediate operational salinity controls.

policies.relationship: Procedural; may affect project choices but not a direct salinity-ops lever
policies.note: Mechanism: CEQA can shape infrastructure/project decisions relevant to salinity management; it does not itself constrain export salinity month-by-month.

Governing Agencies.name: State Water Resources Control Board (SWRCB)
Governing Agencies.note: Adopts/updates the Bay-Delta Plan; sets and enforces water quality objectives; issues/oversees water-right conditions and the compliance framework for Bay-Delta objectives as implemented through decisions like D-1641.

Governing Agencies.name: Regional Water Quality Control Boards (RWQCBs)
Governing Agencies.note: Implement Porter-Cologne regionally (Basin Plans, permits, enforcement) and participate in water quality standards implementation; roles intersect with projects affecting Delta tributaries and water quality.

Governing Agencies.name: California Department of Water Resources (DWR)
Governing Agencies.note: Operates the State Water Project, including the Banks Pumping Plant; coordinates operations in the Bay-Delta to meet applicable water quality requirements and project constraints.

Governing Agencies.name: U.S. Bureau of Reclamation (USBR)
Governing Agencies.note: Operates the Central Valley Project, including the Jones Pumping Plant; coordinates with SWP and complies with applicable water quality requirements, ESA-driven operational constraints, and CVPIA-related operational/restoration requirements.

Governing Agencies.name: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)
Governing Agencies.note: Federal oversight role for Clean Water Act programs including water quality standards framework and certain regulatory authorities; not the day-to-day operator for Delta exports but central to CWA structure.

Governing Agencies.name: California Water Boards — CWA §401 Certification Program (SWRCB/RWQCBs)
Governing Agencies.note: Issues CWA §401 water quality certifications (and conditions/denials) for federally permitted/licensed activities that may discharge to waters, which can include actions affecting Delta hydrodynamics or salinity drivers.

Governing Agencies.name: NOAA Fisheries (NMFS)
Governing Agencies.note: Conducts ESA Section 7 consultations for anadromous salmonids; resulting BiOps can constrain CVP/SWP export operations in ways that indirectly affect Delta flows and salinity intrusion risk.

Governing Agencies.name: U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service (USFWS)
Governing Agencies.note: Participates in ESA implementation for species under its jurisdiction and engages in CVPIA-related fish/wildlife efforts; can influence operational/restoration priorities that indirectly affect export conditions.

Governing Agencies.name: Delta Stewardship Council (DSC)
Governing Agencies.note: Implements the Delta Reform Act’s governance framework via the Delta Plan and consistency process; influences major covered actions that can affect Delta ecosystem and water quality conditions over time.

Governing Agencies.name: California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW)
Governing Agencies.note: Often a CEQA trustee/responsible agency providing input on environmental impacts for projects affecting Delta habitat and conditions; CEQA involvement can shape project design relevant to salinity management (indirectly).

Governing Agencies.name: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE)
Governing Agencies.note: Issues certain federal permits (e.g., dredge/fill) that may trigger CWA processes including §401 certification; can be involved in projects affecting channels/hydrodynamics relevant to salinity intrusion.
